minutes.headline: Planning Board approved every waiver for the 1259 Mass Ave plan and released all but a held-back sum of the Emerald Place bond.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed the 1259 Mass Ave landscaping-facility development plan with the applicant's engineer and the peer review engineer, voted on each waiver with directives, and approved the plan conditional on peer review sign-off. It then voted to return most of the Emerald Place bond, heard an MRPC presentation on the housing production plan, and handled minutes, committee reports and a member's suggestion to make meetings more efficient.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved the 1259 Mass Ave plan, conditional on peer review sign-off, after voting on each waiver in turn.
Most waivers passed with conditions, such as limits on parked vehicles and added dimensions or drain-cover detail on the plans; one vote was not audible in the captions.
The board voted to refund the Emerald Place bond, holding back a portion as an incentive to finish the berms and top coat.
The board set a master plan economic development workshop for October 20 at 6:30 pm and took the village district bylaw hearing off the agenda until a draft exists.
The regional planning commission (MRPC) is to return in September with a less final housing production plan draft for discussion.

why_it_matters: The 1259 Mass Ave conditions on parking, chemical handling and driveway design shape how a landscaping facility operates next to neighbors and the road.
Holding back part of the Emerald Place bond is the town's lever to see the remaining work finished, so the cost of any unfinished work does not fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The housing production plan and village district bylaw are still drafts, and any resulting bylaw would later come to residents as a Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: Peer review sign-off on the 1259 Mass Ave plan, which the approval depends on.
MRPC's September return with a revised housing production plan draft, and the October 20 master plan workshop.
